newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Insinger launches midcap investment fund.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Insinger launches midcap investment fund.

text.p: Bank Insinger de Beaufort in Amsterdam said on Monday it was launching a new investment fund focused at small- and medium-sized Dutch listed companies.

Insinger Emerging Companies Netherlands Fund was set up because investors were relatively cautious about investing in smaller Dutch stocks because of low trading volumes and scarce company information, the investment bank said.
By using a large database and continuous research, Insinger Asset Management was able to start an investment vehicle for these less actively traded stocks, it said in a statement.

Earlier on Monday financial bank/insurance giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) said it was also introducing a mid-cap investment fund in order to cater increased investor demand for these companies.
In addition, Insinger said it had reorganised its other investment funds, totalling 195 million guilders of invested capital today compared with 85 million guilders six months ago.

Funds formerly known under the names of Bemco, Integro or Algemeen Fondsenbezit were now all dubbed Insinger and these comprised seven different Dutch funds, two of which (Global Select and Dynamisch Beheer) would be merged.
Nederland Select was Insinger's best performing fund in the 1996 first half year, yielding a 16 percent return ex-dividend and tracking the rise of the AEX index of 25 major Dutch stocks.
Insinger Nederland Optimaal Select had hedged positions in the first three months of 1996, causing costs that pressured the yield to 11 percent ex-dividend.
The worst performing fund was Insinger RentSelect which gained one percent in value.
